data.description:
# Reserve free-tier request budget for in-progress sessions, and cap the wait at 15s

discovered-from:LP-0MVDQ1GMO00801PL

## Goal (user story)

As the proxy operator, I want an in-progress agent session to almost never wait
for `munitoai-free` capacity, so the budget gate stops adding tens of seconds to
every turn of an established session — while new sessions keep passing straight
through to the next tier exactly as they do today.

## Problem (measured, 2026-10-18)

`LP-0MVDQ1GMO00801PL` shipped a 60 s maximum wait for *in-progress* sessions (a
session that has already been served by the gated entry). Because affinity is
recorded on the first successful dispatch, **every subsequent turn of that
session is an "in-progress" request**, so the wait path applies to nearly all
established traffic rather than being a rare exception.

One hour of post-gate traffic (`/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log`, 13:05:09 →
14:06:19, measured for `LP-0MVDU4FDE003RQHS`):

| Metric | Baseline 6 h | Since the gate |
|---|---|---|
| Free-tier **generation** duration p50 / p95 | 1.3 s / 12.5 s | 1.8 s / 13.5 s |
| **First-token** latency p90 / p95 / p99 | 6.5 s / 10.8 s / **20.9 s** | 12.8 s / 21.5 s / **52.9 s** |
| Budget waits | — | 46 (p50 13.5 s, p90 43.1 s, 12 waits of **30–60 s**) |

The model is not slower — the loss is entirely pre-dispatch waiting. Operator
observation that triggered this item: *"I'm worried that we are waiting too long
on responses from the free tier, everything seems slow."*

## Desired change

1. **Reserve** part of each gated entry's window for in-progress sessions:
   requests from sessions **without** affinity may consume at most
   `rate_limit_rpm - reserve` slots per rolling 60 s window, where
   `reserve = floor(rate_limit_rpm * server.provider_rate_limit_reserve_ratio)`
   (new config key, default `0.3`; for `rate_limit_rpm: 10` that reserves 3
   slots → new sessions capped at 7, affinity sessions may use all 10).
   Sessions **with** affinity may use the full `rate_limit_rpm`.
2. **Clamp the reserve** so it can never lock new sessions out entirely:
   `reserve` is at least 0 and at most `rate_limit_rpm - 1` (so `rpm: 1` reserves
   0; a ratio of 1.0 still leaves one slot for new sessions). An unset/zero ratio
   disables the reserve (today's behaviour).
3. **Lower the wait cap** `server.provider_rate_limit_wait_max_seconds` from 60
   to **15** so any residual wait cannot dominate a turn.
4. Keep every existing guarantee: new sessions never wait; affinity sessions that
   still cannot get a slot after the (now 15 s) cap pass through; waiters are
   depth-capped and disconnect-abortable; the gate fails open when unset; per-entry
   budgets and affinity stay per provider entry.

Not in scope: streaming wait feedback (SSE comment while waiting) — tracked as a
follow-up; and any change to `rate_limit_rpm` itself.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Reserve applied:** with `rate_limit_rpm: 10` and
   `provider_rate_limit_reserve_ratio: 0.3`, a new-session request is refused
   once 7 dispatches are in the rolling window, while an affinity-session
   request is still dispatched (8th–10th slot).
2. **Clamping:** `rpm: 1` reserves 0; ratio `1.0` leaves exactly one slot for new
   sessions; ratio `0`/unset reproduces today's behaviour (new sessions may use the
   whole window); reserve is never ≥ `rpm`.
3. **Worst-case latency bounded:** with the shipped config the maximum budget wait
   is 15 s (config value) and no wait exceeds it; an affinity session that still
   cannot get a slot passes through with reason `rate_limited_after_wait`.
4. **Unchanged guarantees preserved:** new sessions still never wait (no
   `session_affinity=false` wait events), waits remain depth-capped and abort on
   client disconnect, and an entry without `rate_limit_rpm` is still ungated.
5. **Observability:** skip/wait log lines and the recorded attempt diagnostics
   expose the effective new-session cap (limit) and the recorded reserve, so the
   operator can see whether the reserve is being used; the provider diagnostics
   table keeps showing remaining/limit.
6. **Unit + integration tests** cover AC1–AC4 (reserve boundary for new vs affinity
   sessions; clamping cases; wait cap 15 s; disconnect abort still works;
   interleaved new/affinity traffic through both fallback entry points).
7. **Documentation** updated: `proxy/config.yaml` comments, `proxy/README.md`,
   `proxy/docs/routing.md` (behaviour table + reserve explanation), and
   `proxy/MODEL_ADD.md` (`rate_limit_rpm` section) — including the new
   `provider_rate_limit_reserve_ratio` key.
8. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/proxy/provider_budget.py` — reserve computation + apply the reduced cap to
  new sessions; log/expose it in `BudgetDecision`.
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — pass the reserve through (config read), record it in
  attempt diagnostics; `format_budget_status` wording if needed.
- `proxy/config.yaml` — `provider_rate_limit_reserve_ratio: 0.3`,
  `provider_rate_limit_wait_max_seconds: 15`, plus commented documentation.
- `proxy/tests/test_provider_budget.py` — reserve/clamping/wait-cap cases.
- `proxy/tests/test_config_merge.py` + `proxy/tests/fixtures/merged_config_*.json`,
  `prededup_raw_*.json` — golden fixtures for the new/changed server keys.
- `proxy/tests/test_munitoai_fallback_chain.py` — no change expected (entry-level
  `rate_limit_rpm` unchanged); verify only.
- `proxy/README.md`, `proxy/docs/routing.md`, `proxy/MODEL_ADD.md` — documentation.

## Related work

- `LP-0MVDQ1GMO00801PL` (completed, in_review) — the budget gate being refined.
- `LP-0MVDU4FDE003RQHS` (open, scheduled 02:05) — full-window effectiveness
  evaluation; its numbers will be re-read after this change (the wait cap and the
  reserve both move).
- `LP-0MVDNP36J006430L` (open) — header-derived budgeting.

data.comment:
## Implementation notes

**Reserve (AC1/AC2).** `provider_budget.reserved_slots(rpm, config)` = `min(floor(rpm * provider_rate_limit_reserve_ratio), rpm - 1)`, 0 when `rpm <= 1` or the ratio is 0. `acquire_provider_budget()` now applies a per-request cap: in-progress sessions (affinity) use the full `rate_limit_rpm`; new/anonymous sessions use `new_session_limit()` = `rpm - reserve` (7 of 10 with the shipped values). The limiter's single sliding window plus these per-caller caps make the reserve exact and race-free.

**Wait cap (AC3).** `_DEFAULT_WAIT_MAX_SECONDS` 60 → **15**; `provider_rate_limit_wait_max_seconds: 15` in `config.yaml`. An in-progress session that still cannot get a slot after 15 s passes through (`rate_limited_after_wait`).

**Observability (AC5).** `BudgetDecision` gains `reserve_slots`/`effective_limit`; both fallback entry points record them in the attempt diagnostics and the skip log now reads `... limit=7 reserve=3 remaining=3 reason=rate_limited session_affinity=false`.

**Tests.** 7 new cases in `test_provider_budget.py` (reserve boundary new vs in-progress, ratio 0 = previous behaviour, rpm=1 and ratio 1.0 clamping, 15 s default cap, wait-wins-inside-cap, no new-session waiting, log/diagnostics fields, end-to-end 8th-session→paid-tier) plus the legacy `test_rate_limiter.py` integration expectation updated for the reserve (4 of 5 slots for an anonymous session, 1 reserved) with the reason inline.

**Config/docs/fixtures.** `provider_rate_limit_reserve_ratio: 0.3` added (inherited-only key, so golden merge fixtures + `BASE_ONLY_SERVER_KEYS` updated); `proxy/README.md`, `proxy/docs/routing.md` (behaviour table + 'why the reserve exists' with the measured latency numbers) and `proxy/MODEL_ADD.md` updated.
